_why: This plugin paraphrases rules from skills it does not own. A rule can change upstream while our prose keeps describing the old one -- a quiet failure the SKILLS: MISSING line cannot catch, because the skill is present and loads fine. Pinning the exact version our prose was written against makes that drift detectable.

skills.name: tdd
skills.author: Matt Pocock
charactersedRules: implementation-coupled: verifying through a side channel, e.g. querying the database instead of using the interface
tautological: expected values must come from an independent source of truth, not recomputed the way the code does
horizontal slicing: writing all tests first, then all implementation; work in vertical slices
red before green; one slice at a time; refactoring is not part of the loop
seams: the public boundary you observe behaviour at, and no test at an unconfirmed seam

knownEquivalent.note: Differs from the pin by one line: 'use the /codebase-design skill' became 'call the Skill tool with "codebase-design"'. A mechanism change in the upstream skill's own prose; it touches none of the rules this plugin characterises, so paraphrases written against either version are accurate.

skills._equivalenceRule: A hash belongs here only after someone has read the diff and confirmed it changes no characterised rule. It is a record that the check was done, not a way to silence the warning.
